additional_info.body:
Dear colleagues,
Mr. Romain from Engie raised this ticket there are 3 topics open.
PowerConverter[3] - SN:
2102312VGQKXN7001002SA012200000204FW:DC116PF116H100
has E:32 which is to be replaced
DC3 and DC4 groups are not receiving the 12V fast shutdown, please check if QA34 and QA35 are being closed, if you can check 24V between A1:A2 if they are closed and then 11-14. If they receive 24V but are not closing then it's possibly the switch that is broken. Please bring to site 2 extra QA34/35.
PowerConverter[14] is not found, CAN communication error
From this photo below please check which SN is missing and that is the converter, also bring a spare converter in case we cannot fix it. The first thing to try is to swap this converter with the neighbour to see if there is a cabling issue or converter issue.
If the non-working converter now works in the new position and the other too, then it means that it was a cabling issue somewhere in the CAN line
If the non-working converter now works in the new position and the working one doesn't work then it means that there is a cabling issue
If the non-working converter still doesn't work in the new position then that means that it's faulty and needs replacement.

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0394107-DC/Si-D/FR[X0lnqs] - Fastshutdown failed in DC3/4 CRM:00315002166
additional_info.body:
Good morning colleagues,
I am reaching out regarding ticket
ID0394107.
The ticket was opened for issues on Power Converters and Fastshutdown failing on DC3 and DC4 for charger
X0Inqs.
I had a look at the previous activity and I aligned with Francois, who managed the ticket before me. From my understanding:
Two power converters were found defective. These power converters have been disconnected and the number of PCs has been adjusted on SCB. DC1 and DC3 have each one power converter less configured now.
Measurements on the Fastshutdown line have been conducted and it was verified that the 12V signal for fastshutdown arrives correctly.
Several other components have been replaced.
I had a look at the charger in these days, and it seems to me that
a wrong configuration of the converters might have been created onsite
. I forced the converter grouping remotely and I checked with the debug station (see video attached). This is also the current error flags on the power converters:
What I can see is:
Two power converters are not found, as stated above, and this could be correct.
Power converter [0] (
SN: 2102312VGQLUP8001033) is not allocated. This results in one converter less in DC3 (which now has only 2 PC instead of the 3 configured). As you can see from the video, the converter is powered on, but it is not allocated. Maybe the CAN communication cables are not connected properly?
Power converter [12] (SN: 2102312VGQKXN7001194) is allocated, but during the fastshutdown phase it is powered on, it immediately switches off and cannot be powered on anymore. It seems to me that this PC behaves exactly as if it is connected to DC1 Converter Group, instead of DC3.
I do not see any issue with the SMC contactors, as all of them are commanded correctly.
In conclusion, in my eyes it seems that there might be some wrong wiring of the Power converters. It could be that some power converters might be disconnected, or some power converters are connected to the wrong cables. I believe that an onsite visit is required and the connections to the power converters must be verified.
Please let me know in advance if you require support.
Looking forward to hearing from you soon!
With kind regards,

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0394107-DC/Si-D/FR[X0lnqs] - Fastshutdown failed in DC3/4 CRM:00315002166
additional_info.body:
Good morning Franck,
I am reaching out regarding ticket
ID0394107
for fastshutdown failed on DC3 and DC4 on charger
X0Inqs
.
I saw your notes from last week regarding the replacement of the power converters. Now all the power converters are grouped correctly, and the issue stands only in the fastshutdown.
Attached to this email I send you the video from the debug station of the converter grouping and fastshutdown phase on the charger. As it is possible to see from the video, and checking the electric schemes:
Converter grouping phase happens correctly. All the power converters are grouped without reporting issues and all the Switching Matrix Contactors are grouped correctly.
The issue appears when the fastshutdown signal has to reach DC4. Since the charger has no dispenser, the fastshutdown of DC3 and DC4 is just a forwarding of 12V signal through the relays QA33-QA34 and QA35.
I believe that the issue could rely either on the QA33 or in the connection on F03-XD6 after the QA33.
I believe that either the contacts 11-12-14 of the QA33 are not working, or the signal is lost in F03-XD6.9B.
From the converter grouping we see that the other contacts (A1-A2) on QA33 are working fine, as the SMC QA11-12 is closed correctly. It seems that the signal never reaches QA34, so commanding the closure of SMC QA17-18 and the subsequent fastshutdown.
In conclusion, an onsite visit is needed, to measure and verify where the signal is lost. Please organize the onsite visit and bring with you some spare cables, WAGO clamps and multimeter with crocodile probes, so to measure signals. If you already have a spare QA33 or QA34, you can already bring it onsite.
Let me know when you plan to go onsite, so that we can organize a remote session support. I am looping in this email also Francois, as next week I will be traveling onsite and he might step in for the onsite support in case I will not be available.
Looking forward to hearing form you soon!

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0394107-DC/Si-D/FR[X0lnqs] - Fastshutdown failed in DC3/4 CRM:00315002166
additional_info.body:
Good morning everyone,
Today Franck was onsite for charger
X0Inqs
. Firstly we checked that all the dip-switches of the State Monitor KF13 were correctly configured. We checked for false contacts in XD6 and QA32-33-34-35.
We then checked the fastshutdown 12V signal, as I suspected it was interrupted somewhere. We measured the voltage in XD6.10D during fastshutdown phase, and saw that the 12V signal was not reaching that point. QA33 was not probably closing its contact, and therefore the signal was not passing through the other converters groups.
By replacing the relay QA33, the charger configured correctly. Fastshutdown phase was correctly performed and in XD6.10D we could see the 12V signal coming.
Charger is now performing the fastshutdown phase correctly, and all 4 converter groups are now available for charging. No other error flag is present.
Thank you again Franck for your support onsite. We will proceed to close this ticket.

additional_info.subject: Handover from ES to NOC
additional_info.body:
Problem Description
:  Fastshutdown of DC3 and DC4 failed.
Suspected Root Cause
:  Lost 12V signal or faulty component
Action Performed (ES)
:  Logs analysis. At first, checked converters configuration, as some converters were reporting critical errors and were not connected correctly. Analyzed remotely the fastshutdownphase and saw that the SMC contactors were commanded corrcetly, but the fastshutdown signal was not reaching CG4. Onsite visit with remote support identified that the fastshutdown signal was not reaching XD6.10D.
By replacing QA33 issue solved, and charger is now able to complete fastshutdown on all 4 CGs.
Charger SW Version
: v6.0.3
Reason for Handover (ES/NOC
): Issue is solved. Please close the ticket
